transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it — after-hours intake calls are hitting voicemail. What made you start looking to fix this right now?
User: We want to increase our client bookings by ensuring no potential clients are missed after hours.
Agent: Makes sense — if those after-hours calls hit voicemail, bookings slip away. When a call comes in after you’re closed, do people usually leave a message, or do they just call the next clinic?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail, but most would book if someone answered.
Agent: Yeah, that’s a lot of bookings left on the table if it’s ~12 a week. What kind of business is this—are you a vet clinic, medical office, or something else?
User: We're a personal injury law firm, 'Bell & Associates Legal', based in New York, NY.
Agent: Got it — Bell & Associates Legal, PI in New York, and those after-hours calls are going to voicemail. When someone does leave a voicemail, how long does it usually take your team to call them back?
User: We aim to call back the next business day, but it can sometimes take longer due to workload.
Agent: Yeah, that delay can be brutal in PI—people call whoever answers first. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed after-hours calls could be costing you?
User: Sure, that would be helpful to understand the potential impact of those missed calls.
Agent: Perfect — so first number: of those after-hours calls, about how many per week hit voicemail… still around 12?
User: Yes, about 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: Got it — 12 a week. Of those, what percent do you think would actually book a consult if someone answered—half, 60%, 70%?
User: About 70% would book if someone answered the call.
Agent: Makes sense. And for PI, what’s a conservative average value per signed case for you—are we talking $5,000, $10,000, $20,000?
User: Our average intake value is about $1,800 per signed case.
Agent: Got it — at 12 missed calls/week, ~70% booking, and $1,800 per signed case, that’s about **$65,400/month** in potentially recoverable revenue. Cool. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough — I’ll show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow would be better for me.
Agent: Got it — tomorrow works. What time tomorrow is best for you?
User: Anytime in the afternoon would work best for me. Do you have availability then?
Agent: Yeah — afternoon should be fine. Before I pull up times, what time zone should I use for you: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Eastern Time, please.
Agent: Perfect — Eastern time. What’s your first name?
User: I'd prefer to keep it to the firm name for now. We're 'Bell & Associates Legal'.
Agent: No worries — Bell & Associates Legal works. And is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number to reach me is +19172120001.
Agent: Got it — and just to be sure, the best contact number is 9-1-7-2-1-2-0-0-0-1, right? What’s the best first and last name to put on the invite?
User: Yes, that's correct. Just use 'Bell & Associates Legal' for the invite.
Agent: Got it — I’ll put it under Bell & Associates Legal, and +1 (917) 212‑0001 is the best number. For scheduling, I do need a first and last name on the invite—what should I use?
User: Just use the name 'Marcus Bell' for the invite.
Agent: Yep — tomorrow afternoon I can do **2:00 PM** or **2:45 PM** Eastern; which works?
User: 2:00 PM Eastern works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Marcus — you’re booked for **tomorrow at 2:00 PM Eastern**. You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to—anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Thank you for confirming.
Agent: You’ve got it — really glad you called. Jay’s looking forward to speaking tomorrow at 2:00 PM Eastern, and you’ll get that SMS confirmation shortly. Have a great rest of your day — bye!
